nahhas-irab:10-10.t: The original is تتلهّى, i.e. you busy yourself [with something else]. He ﷺ did this seeking the polytheist's acceptance of Islam.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [ذَكَرَهُ is masculine] because it is a non-real feminine. [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun refers to تذكرة, whose feminine gender is grammatical, not real.]

nahhas-irab:13-15.t: It was said: by it [the honoured pages] is meant the Preserved Tablet. This is according to the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās, because Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from him concerning the meaning of بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ (15) that they are the angels. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from him that they are the scribes. Qatāda said: they are the reciters. The correct view is the first; it is well known in the speech of the Arabs that one says سفر الرجل بين القوم when he went as an envoy between them to make peace. The angels are سفرة because they are the messengers of Allah the Exalted to His prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and they are also scribes who record the deeds of the servants. So all this is not contradictory — except that Wahb ibn Munabbih said: السّفرة الكرام البررة are the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ. بررة is the plural of بارّ, and أبرار is the plural of برّ.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Mujāhid said: When Allah the Exalted says "man has been killed (قتل الإنسان)", or [something else] was done to him, it is the disbeliever. The meaning of قتل is "destroyed", because the one killed is destroyed. It was also said: قتل means "cursed". ما أكفره: it is preferable that «ما» be interrogative, i.e. "what has made him disbelieve", despite the manifestness of the signs of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and His favour to him. It was also said: it is an exclamation (taʿajjub).

nahhas-irab:18-20.t: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ: i.e. he was only created from something filthy, and he only becomes noble through obedience to Allah. The best of what has been said about the meaning of ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ (20) is the view of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, that He made it easy for him, i.e. made it easy for him until he came out of the womb. The implied form in Arabic is "then for the way", the lām being omitted because it is a verb that takes two objects, one of them by means of a particle.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: أَنْ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. لأن ("because"). Some grammarians say: its position is genitive, by an implied lām. And some of them say: «أن» means «إذ» ("when").

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
That is, He made him one who has a grave, i.e. [He ordered] that he be buried. As for the one who buries, he is called قابر, as the poet said: [al-sarīʿ] 539-
لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها ... عاش ولم يتنقل إلى قابر»
(If she leaned a dead man against her throat, he would live and not be carried to a burier.) [Translator's note: the source has a stray closing «»» after the verse, and reads يتنقل where the verse is usually cited as ينقل.]

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
That is, He brings him to life; the implied form is "when He wills, He will raise him". One says أنشره الله فنشر ("Allah revived him and he revived"), so he is منشر and ناشر, as the poet said: [al-sarīʿ] 540-
حتّى يقول النّاس ممّا رأوا ... يا عجبا للميّت النّاشر
(Until people say, from what they have seen: How wondrous is the dead man come back to life!)

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: Some grammarians make «كلّا» a complete stop (tamām) throughout the whole Qur'an, i.e. "No! The matter is not as the disbeliever says, 'I have fulfilled what was due from me.'" Some grammarians make it a beginning [of a new sentence] throughout the whole Qur'an, and some distinguish [case by case]. This will be explained under the complete stops (al-tamām), Allah willing.

nahhas-irab:24-26.t:
[إِلى طَعامِهِ] is a complete stop (tamām) according to the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr [إِنَّا]; according to the reading of the Kufans it is not a complete stop, because they read أَنَّا, meaning لأنّا ("because We"). It cannot be a badal (substitute) for طعام as Abū ʿUbayd interpreted it, because the grammarians have set out the kinds of badal and this does not come under them.
The meaning of صَبًّا and شَقًّا is tawkīd (emphasis), and likewise these maṣdars (verbal nouns).

nahhas-irab:27-31.t: It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said in the presence of ʿUmar: The plants of the earth are seven. [ʿUmar] said to him: I do not understand what you are saying. He said: فَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها حَبًّا (27) وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً (28) وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلًا (29) وَحَدائِقَ غُلْباً (30) — i.e. intertwined — وَفاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا (31) — i.e. pasture for the livestock. ʿUmar said: This is how you should speak, as this young man speaks. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from him: الأبّ is what is soft among the fruits. [Translator's note: «ما لأن» in the source is read as «ما لان».]

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The original is يتزكّى; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: [مَتاعاً is] accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [الصَّاخَّةُ is] the Resurrection. ʿIkrima said: the first blast. Al-Ḥasan said: everything listens intently (يصيخ) to it, i.e. everything falls silent for it.

nahhas-irab:34-36.t: It was said: they flee because of the claims they have against one another, and they fear that. It was also said: they flee because they are ashamed before one another and dislike that [the other] should see the disgrace that befalls him.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: That is, it occupies him so that he cannot attend to others.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ: [وجوه] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), even though it is indefinite, because of the information it carries; the khabar (predicate) is مُسْفِرَةٌ.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: [ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ are] naʿt (adjective). Ibn Zayd said: القترة is the dust that rises up. It is related that when the beasts are told, "Become dust", that dust becomes a dust-cloud (غبرة) on the faces of the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
The original is يتذكر; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl because of its closeness to it. فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى: al-Farrāʾ claimed that the accusative is permissible but was not read. Abū Jaʿfar said: The transmission is well known from ʿĀṣim that he read فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى in the accusative. The Kufans say: it is an answer to لعلّ, while the Basrans do not recognise an answer to لعلّ in the accusative. They and the Kufans have both reported what requires the accusative, namely the command, the prohibition, the negation, the wish and the question; the Kufans added the supplication; and they did not mention the answer to لعل among these answers. I asked Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about it, and he said: I know no justification for the accusative, even though ʿĀṣim, with his eminence, read it — except that «أو» may make what follows it accusative, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 538-
فقلت له لا تبك عينك إنّما ... نحاول ملكا أو نموت فنعذرا
(I said to him: let not your eye weep; we are only seeking a kingdom, or we die and are excused.)
So it may be that it is conjoined to what is made accusative after «أو». [Translator's note: the connection to أو is not explained further in the source.]

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: هم may be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) or a mubtadaʾ (subject); الْفَجَرَةُ is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of أولئك.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَّدَّى is the reading of the Medinans; the original is تتصدّى, then it was assimilated. The reading of the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr is تَصَدَّى with the omission of a tāʾ, so as not to combine two tāʾs. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings as «تَصَدَّى»; the Medinan reading, by the explanation given, has the doubled ṣād.]

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: [يَسْعى] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: [وَهُوَ يَخْشى]. It is also possible that the clause is another khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: this entry continues the sentence of the previous one.]
